subject: Culture
title: Fantasy Coffins of Ghana
description: A quick win: understand Fantasy Coffins of Ghana.

hook.text: In Ghana, a fisherman might be buried in a coffin shaped like a giant fish. A pilot gets an airplane coffin.

buildup.text: The Ga people of Accra believe the afterlife continues your earthly identity. Your coffin advertises who you were.

discovery.text: Seth Kane Kwei started the tradition in the 1950s. His grandmother wanted to fly, so he built her a cocoa pod coffin.

twist.text: Fantasy coffins now sell to art collectors worldwide for up to $20,000. Death art became a global export.

climax.text: The coffins celebrate life rather than mourning death. Every burial is a public display of achievement.

punchline.text: Your last bed should tell your best story.

quiz.question: Who started Ghana's fantasy coffin tradition?
